value: Moravian Frankovka is firm with acidity and tannin when young, showing blackberry and dark spice, and turns velvety with age.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: young wines acidic and tannic, mature ones spicy with blackberry and cinnamon, velvety texture. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: plums, cherries, blackberries, black spice; full with higher tannin, becomes velvety and soft with ageing.

value: Moravian Chardonnay is crisp on cooler sites, with orchard fruit and white flowers, and riper and creamier on warmer ones.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: cooler sites give crisp acidity, green apple and acacia flowers; warmer sites mango and cream. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: orchard or citrus fruit, white flowers, roasted nuts or honey; pronounced acids in youth.

value: Moravian Tramín červený from ripe grapes is full and opulent, almost viscous, with exotic fruit and sweet spice around its rose scent.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: tea rose aroma; wines from ripe grapes full and opulent with a concentrated viscous structure. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: exotic fruits, sweet spices, tea rose, honey.

value: Moravian Ryzlink vlašský is fresh and juicy with gooseberry and currant notes, and takes on honeyed tones from riper grapes or with age.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: fresh, full, balanced; currants or gooseberry, honeyed notes in mature wines. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: gooseberry, red currant, meadow flowers; juicy and fresh with good acidity; honey or raisin tones from well ripened grapes.

value: In Moravia it is zesty with firm acidity and a peppery spice, and its weight depends much on the ripeness of the year.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: zingy and refreshing depending on the year's ripeness, white pepper spice. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: pepper and spice, light minerality, juicy, fresh, strong acidity.

value: In Moravia it is gently muscat scented with peach notes, fresh and lively on the palate.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: muscat scent with nettle and peach, medium to full bodied, lively. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: mildly aromatic with light nutmeg and peach or grapefruit; fresh, moderately full, juicy.

value: A Moravian crossing of Muscat Ottonel and Prachttraube, bred to give local growers a grape with a muscat scent.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: origin Morava wine region, crossing Muscat Ottonel x Prachtraube. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: bred by V. Křivánek at Polešovice from Muscat Ottonel and Prachttraube because there was no suitable muscat scented variety for Czech regions.

value: Light and delicately aromatic, with floral muscat scents, tangerine and orange, and a fine acidity that keeps it balanced.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: delicately aromatic with fine acidity, nose of tangerines and oranges. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: floral, muscatty aromas, light wines with balance when acidity is sufficient; page summary mentions flowers and tropical fruit.

value: A Moravian crossing of Gewürztraminer and Müller Thurgau that makes full, aromatic whites.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: origin Morava wine region, Gewürztraminer x Müller Thurgau; full bodied. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: bred by Josef Veverka from Gewürztraminer and Müller Thurgau; aromatic.

value: Full and long, it recalls its parent Tramín červený in scent, with roses, exotic fruit and sweet spice.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: full bodied, long finish, lychee, mandarin, nutmeg and vanilla. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: aroma mostly of parent Gewürztraminer: roses, sweet spices, exotic fruit; long lasting taste.

value: Moravian Rulandské bílé is full and elegant with a delicate floral nose, gaining pear and hazelnut notes as it matures.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: elegant, full bodied, delicate floral scent maturing to ripe pears, red fruit and hazelnuts. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: delicate fruit and floral aroma, pears, bread crust and hazelnuts in mature wine; full, elegant.

value: In Moravia it is made full and smooth, with ripe, rounded fruit.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: full bodied palate with ample, smooth flavours, red orange and honey. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: fuller, harmonious, fruity, exotic and orchard fruit, long aftertaste.

value: Moravian Rulandské modré is pale and fresh with strawberry and red berry fruit when young, and turns to leather, smoke and dried plum with age.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: pale ruby to brick red; with maturation leather, smoke, strawberries, dried plums. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: forest fruits, raspberries, strawberries; older wines leather, smoke, prunes; young wines have spicy acidity that softens.

value: Moravian Ryzlink rýnský leans to ripe apricot with linden and other floral notes, full bodied yet refreshing.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: ripe apricots, linden flowers and quince. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: peaches, apricots or citrus young, flowery and honey tones older; full, refreshing, spicy acidity.

value: Moravian Sauvignon is spicy and zesty, often with a note of nettle, moving toward riper fruit in warmer years.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: intensely aromatic and spicy with zesty acidity, from grass and nettles to orchard fruit. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: nettles, dandelion, herbs in young wines; ripe grapes give blackcurrant, gooseberry, peach; slightly spicy.

value: Besides aged reds, it is one of the main grapes for Svatomartinské, the young St Martin's wine.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: the Czech answer to Beaujolais Nouveau, released as St Martin's wine; older bottles become velvety. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: one of the main varieties used for St Martin's young wine.

value: Moravian Svatovavřinecké is juicy with sour cherry and plum, its brisk acidity softening to velvet with age.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: sour cherry, plum jam, sometimes blackcurrant; older bottles velvety. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: stone fruit, plums, jam, cinnamon; juicy, fruity, strong acidity that softens and becomes velvety with maturation.

value: Moravian Zweigeltrebe is spicy, with cherry and blackberry fruit.
source_notes: National Wine Centre (Národní vinařské centrum), national Czech variety guide; Moravia holds the large majority of Czech vineyards: bouquet of various spices and fruits, often berry fruit. Wine Fund (Vinařský fond) Wines from Czech Republic encyclopedia: cherries and other berries; spicy; blackberries, cherries, forest fruits.

value: Tokaj's main grape and one of the six the rules allow, used for everything from bone dry whites to Aszú and Eszencia, often blended with Hárslevelű.
source_notes: Tokaj Wine Region Council text on the Tokaj tourism site: Furmint is the region's primary and main variety, good at noble rotting. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): makes bone dry to Essencia, botrytis basis of Aszú, blended with Hárslevelű. Tokaj PDO specification VI: six permitted varieties (applicant is the same council, so counted with the council).

value: On Tokaj's volcanic soils its dry wines are crisp and mineral, and in sweet wines its high acidity keeps the sugar in balance.
source_notes: Wine Folly: dry Furmint crisp and mineral; sweet Tokaji's bright acidity balances the sugar. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): high acidity, neutral dry wines reflect terroir. Tokaj council: good acid preserving abilities.

value: Tokaj's other main grape, made on its own or blended with Furmint in dry and sweet wines, where its softer acidity rounds out Furmint.
source_notes: Tokaj council: the other decisive variety, adequate acids but fewer than Furmint, helps its companions; less prone to aszú. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): important in Aszú and dry wines, alone or blended with Furmint, refining its acidity.

value: In Tokaj it is softer and more perfumed than Furmint, with a scent of linden honey.
source_notes: Tokaj council: linden honey, sometimes elderflower odour; fewer acids than Furmint. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): linden blossom and linden blossom honey, soft acidity; in Tokaj complements Furmint's acidity with delicate aromatics.

value: One of the six grapes Tokaj's rules allow, made into dry wines and, in exceptional years, even into Aszú made from it alone.
source_notes: Tokaj council: intermediate variety, demanding on soil, aszú can be harvested from it in exceptional vintages. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): in Tokaj makes dry wines and sometimes Aszú made entirely from it. Specification VI lists it among the six permitted grapes.

value: In Tokaj it keeps a higher acidity than Muscat Ottonel, so its scented wines stay fresh.
source_notes: Tokaj council: acidity content higher, odour not comparable with Ottonel muscat. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): fresh acidity, grape blossom and violet aromas, best young for primary aromas.

value: One of the four traditional Somló grapes allowed in the Superior category, alone or blended with the others.
source_notes: Somló PDO specification (version 2): Superior only from furmint, hárslevelű, juhfark, olasz rizling or blends in any proportion. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu) Somló page: superior category permits only traditional Somló varieties Furmint, Hárslevelű, Juhfark, Olaszrizling.

value: One of the four traditional Somló grapes allowed in the Superior category, alone or blended with the others.
source_notes: Somló PDO specification: Superior only from furmint, hárslevelű, juhfark, olasz rizling. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): same four traditional Somló varieties for the superior category.

value: One of the four traditional Somló grapes allowed in the Superior category, alone or blended with the others.
source_notes: Somló PDO specification: Superior only from furmint, hárslevelű, juhfark, olasz rizling. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): same four traditional Somló varieties for the superior category.

value: On Somló it is lean and piercingly acidic when young, with a smoky, ashy edge, and gains richness with bottle age.
source_notes: Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): Somló wines young show citrus, herbs, stony leanness and piercing acidity; quality improves over time. Wine Folly: ashy, savory and fierce, lemon and smoke, gains golden richness with age. Decanter sponsored piece (supporting only): weighty, vivid acidity, ageing potential.

value: A historic Badacsony grape, and one of the traditional varieties allowed in the hill named wines.
source_notes: Badacsony PDO specification (version 2): Badacsonyi furmint was one of five protected Badacsony wines in the 1936 wine law; Furmint is listed for hill named white wines. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): Furmint was the main variety in the 18th century before Olaszrizling gained ground.

value: An old native grape found almost only in Badacsony, revived after nearly vanishing, usually made dry and allowed in the hill named wines.
source_notes: Badacsony PDO specification: ancient autochthonous variety typical only of the region, the once famous almost forgotten Kéknyelű was brought back into cultivation; listed for hill named whites. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): essentially only found in Badacsony, generally produced dry.

value: In Badacsony it is lean and sharply acidic when young, with a salty, slightly oily texture, and needs a year or two in bottle to open up.
source_notes: Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): restrained fruit and spice, leanness, salty oily texture, piercing acidity, benefits from a year or two of bottle age. Badacsony specification: Badacsony wines generally have slightly salty notes from basalt (not grape specific). Decanter sponsored piece: crunchy, understated young, honeyed smoky richness with age.

value: One of Badacsony's three traditional leading grapes with Olaszrizling and Kéknyelű, and allowed in the hill named wines.
source_notes: Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): traditionally three leading varieties, Olaszrizling, Szürkebarát (Pinot Gris) and Kéknyelű. Badacsony specification: Szürkebarát planted after phylloxera, its name has become fused with Badacsony; listed for hill named whites.

value: An important red in Villány for centuries, made on its own and allowed alongside Portugieser in the light Redy blend.
source_notes: Villány PDO specification (version 5): Kékfrankos spread in the 18th century and is still an important variety; Redy must be 51 to 66 percent Kékoportó with 20 to 49 percent Blauburger, Kadarka, Kékfrankos, Zweigelt. Wine Folly: a native red also grown in Villány. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): planted on Villány's cooler Várerdő slope.

value: In Villány's warm south it is riper and rounder than in cooler places, with plum, wild strawberry and sloe, and jammy, dried fruit notes in the top wines.
source_notes: Villány specification, Super Premium (100 percent Cabernet Franc): sloe, wild strawberry and plum typical of Cabernet Franc, dried fruit and jam, Villány roundness. Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): in Villány forest fruits, a hint of jam, warmth and ripeness, spicy, mellow, full bodied. Wine Folly: polished, velvety, green pepper only a minor note.

value: In Villány it is mostly made light and youthful, with fresh red fruit, soft tannins and lively acidity, for drinking young.
source_notes: Wines of Hungary (bor.hu): Villány Portugieser light, fresh, fruity, often a new wine, sometimes carbonic maceration; Redy youthful and fruity with soft tannins and light body. Villány specification, Classicus vörös Redy (at least 51 percent Kékoportó, the Portugieser vine): playful acidity, at most medium tannin, light body, youthful primary fruit.

value: In Istria it is deeply coloured with firm tannins and a savoury, gamey edge behind the fruit, and it benefits from barrel age.
source_notes: Wine Folly: forest berries and violets with smoky meat and game notes, high tannins. GuildSomm (Miquel Hudin): good tannins that respond well to barrel ageing, can be blocky unless aged. Decanter guide sponsored by Vinistra (supporting): inky purple, firm tannins, rustic savouriness and iron, oak for ageing.

value: Most Istrian Malvazija is made fresh and young in steel, while skin contact and oak give fuller, more textured and gently honeyed versions.
source_notes: GuildSomm: wines range from powerful and heavily oaked to basic, fruity, refreshing and young. Decanter guide sponsored by Vinistra: at least 70 percent vinified in steel for fresh summer drinking; skin contact gives texture; wood suits its gently honeyed, floral character.

value: Along the Dalmatian coast it makes powerful, warm reds that can run very high in alcohol.
source_notes: Wine Folly: rich, higher in alcohol and tannin, lower acidity. GuildSomm: Dingač Plavac Mali can be very high in alcohol; traditionally heavily extracted.

value: A native Croatian white tied above all to the island of Korčula, around Čara and Smokvica, and now also planted on the mainland.
source_notes: GuildSomm: Pošip is a star on Korčula, DNA shows it is native to Croatia, now also found on the mainland. Croatia Week (news site, lower tier): Korčula's indigenous grape centred on Čara and Smokvica.

value: Despite the Dalmatian heat it can make crisp, elegant whites.
source_notes: GuildSomm: despite the region's heat, elegant wines can be made from this grape. Wine Folly: often crisp, with apple, citrus and a subtle almond note.

value: Croatia's best known Traminac comes from Ilok in Srijem, where it is made in styles from dry to sweet late harvest wines.
source_notes: Vina Croatia (wine association of the Croatian Chamber of Economy): the most famous Croatian Traminer is the Ilok Traminer, a leading European Traminer; regular vintages mostly dry. Total Croatia News (lower tier): thrives around Ilok in Srijem; late picked predicate wines and sweet versions.

value: Around Ilok it is rich and full with fairly high alcohol.
source_notes: Vina Croatia: high alcohol levels, complete taste, rich and full; linden and honey notes in dry wines. Total Croatia News (lower tier): usually semi dry with quite high alcohol.

value: In Štajerska Šipon gives bright, crisp wines with pronounced acidity, fuller and more fragrant when the grapes ripen well.
source_notes: Decanter (Caroline Gilby MW): bright, crisp, refreshing wines thanks to sometimes fierce acidity, better ripeness now gives aromatics and fruit; tradition dry. Dušan Terčelj, The Culture of Wine in Slovenia (University of Primorska Press): Šipon gives neutral wines with pronounced acidity, a good low yield vintage gives a full bodied wine with pleasant varietal bouquet.
